slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will unrot
your brain

slow cooking

cook one meal a week from scratch with no recipe video playing. using your hands and real steps brings back the patience that endless short videos slowly took away from you.

a book on paper

read 20 pages of a paper book before bed instead of scrolling. your attention span grows back much faster than you think, and your sleep quietly gets better too.

bird watching

spend 10 minutes a day watching birds from a window or a park bench. learning to notice small movements trains a patient kind of focus your feed never asks of you.

one lesson a day

swap 5 minutes of scrolling for 5 minutes of learning: a strange fact about the ocean, a painting, a moment in history. the urge to scroll fades when your brain gets fed something real.
slides.texte_sophia:
one lesson a day

i used to scroll for an hour every night. now i spend 5 minutes on one lesson in the Sophia app instead: the ocean, a painting, a moment in history. my brain finally feels fed.

slides.texte_overlay:
boredom on purpose

sit for 10 minutes a day with nothing: no phone, no music, no book. boredom is where your brain starts making its own ideas again instead of eating everyone else's.
